reason: The answer resolves the apparent conflict exactly as the passages allow: the manual's allegement rule is anchored on 'a period of 5 hours measured backwards from the cut-off time of the FOP (17:00 WET)' [[porto-cancellation-allegement]] §12.4, PDF 133/printed 132, while the operating-hours page prints 'FOP (Free of Payment) cut-off 18:00' under 'T2S Time CET' with 'Please Note: Portugal uses WET (Western European Time), which is -1 hour than CET' [[porto-operating-hours-web]], and the bundle's own LIMITATION 'The FOP cut-off is printed as 17:00 WET here (18:00 CET)' is quoted, so neither source is declared wrong. Both sources are cited with review date 2026-09-14 (sources 2026-09-13 and 2026-09-14), Portuguese governing language, unresolved effective date, reference-description basis, R2026.JUN release, Notice 0394/2024 as binding source and the baseline/overlay LIMITATIONs all preserved; every clock time (16:00, 16:30, 17:40, 17:45, 18:00, the five partial windows, 12:00 noon WET) matches the excerpts. It also correctly notes that the retrieved T2S excerpt [[t2s-rts-phase]] does not itself print an FOP cut-off time (the UDFS section that does was not offered by the bundle) and flags the web table's 'Cycle 5 15:30 – 16:00' against the UDFS '15:30 and 16:05' as a genuine reproduction divergence.
